tasks.set: W-AD78-University Career Preparation and Job Readiness
tasks.title: Academic Discussion
tasks.class: University Career Preparation and Job Readiness
tasks.instruction:
Your professor is teaching a class. Write a post responding to the professor's question.
In your response, you should do the following:
• Express and support your personal opinion.
• Make a contribution to the discussion in your own words.
An effective response will contain at least 100 words.

professor.name: Doctor Smith
professor.text: Recently, we've been discussing how universities can help students prepare for their future careers. Many universities offer services to help students write résumés and search for jobs. However, a major criticism of higher education is that most universities do not do enough to help students prepare for and find work after graduation. Do you agree or disagree that universities should do more to help students prepare for and find jobs? Please explain your opinion.

posts.name: Amy
posts.text: I think universities already do quite a lot to help students find jobs. Many universities have a career services office that offers not only résumé writing and job-search help but also information about opportunities to gain work experience while still attending the university—through internships, for example. Students just need to take advantage of the services their universities already offer.

posts.name: Rory
posts.text: I have read about some universities that require students to gain work experience in their intended career field before they graduate. But those are exceptions. I know many graduates who cannot find a job or cannot perform the required work when they do find a job. They learned theories and some interesting but useless information, but they have almost no real-world skills.
